_meta.description: Rolling registry of recent post generation characteristics. Used to inject differentiation context into future generation prompts, preventing hook repetition, title cadence cloning, and emotional arc duplication. Capped at 30 recent entries per category.
_meta.usage: Read by scripts/lib/generation-memory.js before generation. Written after each successful post creation. Pass result to generate-post.js as differentiation context.

recentHooks.hook: Your eyes aren't even fully open yet, and your thumb already found the phone. You're reading a text about somebody else's problem, three ads, and a headline that spikes your cortisol before your feet
It's Sunday night. Seven tabs open, three of them the same document. You opened your project file on Tuesday, stared at it, closed it, and then somehow watched forty minutes of a video about deep sea

You've got both tabs open right now. ChatGPT on the left, Claude on the right, same prompt pasted into both, and you're squinting at the two outputs trying to decide which robot deserves your twenty b

Most creators do not have an automation problem. They have a collection problem. Fourteen tools, three half-built Zapier flows, a Notion dashboard nobody opens, and a nagging feeling that all of it is

It's Sunday night and you're staring at your content calendar like it's a ransom note. Three reels behind. Newsletter unwritten. That song you actually care about sitting untouched in a folder while y

Play three AI-generated tracks back to back and you already know the feeling. Same glassy pads. Same polite drum bus. Same emotional temperature that never rises above lukewarm. It is like walking int

You paste your idea into ChatGPT, hit enter, and out comes something that sounds like a LinkedIn motivational poster wrote a press release. It's grammatically perfect. It's completely dead. And you si
Your bookmarks folder has 23 AI tools in it. Your credit card gets pinged by four of them every month. And when you sit down to actually make something, you stare at the screen and open none of them.
What if the reason your AI setup keeps collapsing is that you built it backwards?

You opened seven browser tabs, signed up for four AI tools, watched a guy on YouTube promise you a "fully automated content empire," and now you have a graveyard of half-used subscriptions and zero cl

You found a piece you love. Now you have three tabs open ~ an Etsy listing, a gallery page, and the artist's own website ~ and the same painting somehow costs three different amounts depending on wher
Here is a thing nobody says out loud at the frame shop: a digital print can hit you harder than a painting, and a painting can leave you cold.
What if the whole idea that original art is out of your reach was sold to you on purpose?

Picture the last time you stood in a friend's living room and stopped, mid-sentence, because something on their wall grabbed you. Not because it matched the couch. Because it made you feel something y
Have you ever bought a print, hung it up, and felt absolutely nothing? Not disappointment, not delight. Just a flat, neutral hum, like the wall was still blank but now had a rectangle on it.
There is a blank wall in your house that has been blank for two years, and every time you walk past it, you feel a small nag that you keep pushing down.

You scroll a wall of "art" on some giant marketplace, and every piece feels like it came off the same conveyor belt. Beige abstract number 4,000. A motivational quote in a font somebody stole. Nothing
You paid, the excitement wore off, and now you are staring at a login you barely use and a bank statement you do not fully understand. Was it $995 one time? Is there a monthly thing you forgot about?
Picture the room. Hotel ballroom, cold air, a stage lit like a concert, and a five-figure receipt sitting in your inbox before you ever shook a hand. That is the AI Mastermind, the top rung of the AI
Nobody sells you the whole ladder at once. That is the trick.

You bought a course once, watched the first two modules, then let the login rot in a browser bookmark you never opened again. That fear is the real reason you are hunting for exactly what the AI Advan
Free never means free. It means "the first taste is on us."
You finished the free summit, maybe grabbed a Jumpstart resource, and now there's a shiny upsell path pointing at something called AI Mastery. You want to know if it is the real deal or just the next
Try this. Sit in a chair, put your phone in another room, and do nothing for four minutes. No music, no scrolling, no plan. Just sit.

Most people write in a journal and come out the other side more confused than when they started. They fill three pages with worry, close the notebook, and feel exactly the same knot in their chest. If
Here's a question almost nobody asks themselves out loud: when was the last time you knew something before you had evidence for it?
It's 11pm. You've closed the last app. The house is quiet. And your head is still going like a slot machine that won't pay out.
You keep asking other people what you should do, and none of their answers land, because the person who actually knows got buried under 400 open tabs and a phone that never stops buzzing.
The scariest sentence in the self-help world is not "you failed." It is "you can still choose."
Six months ago you had a plan. You remember it vaguely, the way you remember a dream ~ something about a project, a move, a version of you that had it together.
